column8: Tier 1 #5 sparse-MDS residual-dense audit: sparse_first_row[r][0] = mds_0_0 = MDS_CIRC_COL[0] = 1 by construction, so the partial-round s0*first_row[0] mul is identity. Replaced 20 vpmuludq + Mont reduce per perm with plain add. Bitwise-identical (test_plonky3_compatibility passes). Measured -0.73% with p=0.00081 across 12+12 samples (3 paired rounds: -0.79/-1.01/-0.40). Real and significant but below 1.0% gate. CANDIDATE FOR SUB-GATE BUNDLING (Research Principle #5).

Bundle: pw4-7 SIMD identity-mul + sparse_mat_air_16 same identity-mul (AIR side). Predicted compounding to cross 1.0% gate. Measured -0.34% p=0.126 across 12+12 (per-round: +0.29/-0.44/-0.85) — INSIGNIFICANT and WEAKER than pw4-7 alone. The AIR-side change introduces negative-impact variance: new_s0 = state[0] + accumulate gives the codegen worse info than new_s0 = ZERO + accumulate(j=0..16). Lesson: identity-mul-elimination only wins on the SIMD hot path; the AIR path is symbolic/generic and the optimizer handles the *1 differently. Returned to pw4-7-revert baseline.

Bundle attempt 2: pw4-7 SIMD identity-mul + constant-array layout tightening (drop unused [0] of packed_sparse_first_row, drop [15] of packed_sparse_v, rename to packed_sparse_w_hat). Predicted compounding via reduced L1D pressure (40 cache lines saved). Measured -0.73% p=0.000364 (per-round: -0.96/-0.96/-0.28) — IDENTICAL TO pw4-7 ALONE. Layout change contributes 0% beyond the identity-mul removal. Confirms the cache footprint reduction (~2.5 KiB) is below detection threshold on this baseline; the -0.73% is purely the mul-port relief. Still sub-gate; no compounding companion found across 3 attempts (pw4-7/8/9).

Tier 1 #2 delayed Montgomery reduction across partial-round S-box chain (AVX-512 only). Replaced canonical mod-add (vpaddd+vpsubd+vpminud, 3-cycle latency) for `+= rc[r]` with raw vpaddd (1-cycle), leaving s0 in [0, 2P) un-reduced; bound checked that Mont mul tolerates 2P*P < 2^32*P input (since P < 2^31). Measured -0.08% p=0.80 across 12+12 (per-round: -0.81/+0.11/+0.46) — INSIGNIFICANT. Latency saving of ~2 cycles/round * 20 rounds = 40 cycles/perm is hidden by OOO execution; the mod-add was not on the binding critical chain at this baseline. Lesson: source-level latency-reduction predictions overstate impact on Zen 4 with deep OOO window. The mul-port THROUGHPUT (not latency) is the binding constraint, and this change does not reduce mul-port pressure. Structural (+0 pts).

Tier 1 #1 retry: full permute_simd_x2 lockstep + compress_pair_mut wiring across mt-symetric Compression trait, compress_layer pair-chunking, and Poseidon1KoalaBear16 (with pw4-7 identity-mul bundled). Per-element constant scoping (let rc=...; let v_j=...;) intended to address exp6 spill caveat by limiting constant lifetimes. Measured +2.64% p=0.0003 REGRESSION (per-round: +2.73/+5.35/-0.08). Per candidate pool prediction +8-12%; the actual codegen still spilled register state across the A/B paired ops despite source-level scoping. Likely reasons: (a) 2*16=32 state ZMMs leave 0 room for active constants — every constant load forces a state spill; (b) OOO reorder buffer saturates with 2x in-flight ops, hurting throughput rather than helping. Confirms exp6 finding — the redesign approach (streamed reload) does not avoid spills on this compiler/codegen. Structural (+0 pts).

Tier 2 pow_bits rebalance: GRINDING_BITS 16 -> 14 (extends exp5's 18->16 trend). Re-gated with n=7 (28+28 samples): wall-clock -2.92% p=0.000483 — gate would KEEP based on wall-clock alone. HOWEVER measured proof_size: 350.05 KiB (pow_bits=16) -> 367.57 KiB (pow_bits=14) = +5.00% increase. Scoring rule net = throughput_pct - 3 * proof_size_increase_pct = 2.92 - 3*5.00 = -12.08 NEGATIVE. The 3x proof-size penalty dominates the wall-clock gain. DISCARDED per scoring rule (not gate threshold). Lesson: the pow_bits/queries tradeoff is unfavorable beyond exp5's 16. Per-bit reduction of pow_bits costs roughly 2.5% proof size for ~1.5% throughput — score-negative. Higher pow_bits (toward 18) might INCREASE proof size by similar amount but reduce throughput; should be re-explored. Micro discard (+1.0 pt). proof_kib=367.6 logged for first time.

Tier 1 #3 + #5 BUNDLE: scalar-bind 15 s_hi values across the partial-round inner loop (so the compiler keeps them register-resident across 20 rounds), unroll dot_product and rank-1 update over named locals, AND drop sparse_first_row[r][0]=1 identity mul (pw4-7). Profile baseline pinpointed `vmovdqa64 [rsp+0x780+rsi*1], zmm` at 2.22% as hottest line — disassembly confirms this is the rank-1 WRITE to split.s_hi[j] memory slot (NOT a spill: compiler kept s_hi array memory-backed). Rewrite eliminates the per-j store/load by binding to scalars. Measured -1.25% wall-clock p=0.000927 (KEEP, gate crossed). Proof size 348.34 KiB vs baseline 350.05 KiB = -0.5% (algebraic identity, expected unchanged; small diff is noise / PoW nonce length). Net score = 1.25 - 3*(-0.5) = +2.75 POSITIVE. Reset stop counter to 0 per program.md (any keep resets).

Phase 4 pivot to lean_vm subsystem after pw4-13 keep. Apply pw4-13 pattern scalar-bind state and drop identity mul to generate_trace_rows_for_perm AIR trace gen. n=7 measured -1.19% but p=0.087 high variance per-round +5.67/-2.74. n=10 confirms NO SIGNAL +0.23% p=0.473. The same pattern from pw4-13 does not transfer to this site likely because trace_gen has smaller share than predicted or state was already register-resident. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Scalar-bind state across initial full rounds in permute_simd + inline mds_fft butterflies with macro-expanded scalar ops. Same insight as pw4-13 but extended to full-round phase. mds_fft was treating state[16] as memory-backed for 80 ops/round (32 dif_ifft + 16 lambda mul + 32 dit_fft). Macros bt_s neg_dif_s dit_s operate on named locals s_0..s_15. Measured -2.13% wall-clock p=0.000724 KEEP. Proof size 349.83 KiB vs pw4-13 baseline 348.34 = +0.4% noise. Net score = 2.13 - 3*0.4 = +0.93 positive. Compress_mut share drops further; cumulative wins now span full-round FFT and partial-round sparse-MDS. Reset counter to 0.

Apply pw4-15 scalar-binding pattern to TERMINAL full rounds (4 rounds 80 ops/round). n=7 -1.30% p=0.088 high variance n=10 -0.68% p=0.00213 sub-gate. Real but smaller than pw4-15 init-rounds gain -2.13%. Likely because terminal rounds are at end no further phases to chain register residency to AND the state-array write-back happens immediately after. Memory boundary at end-of-permute defeats some of the scalar-binding benefit. SUB-GATE-REAL candidate p<0.01 but mean below 1% threshold. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Bundle pw4-16 terminal rounds scalar binding WITH scalar-binding through last-initial fused mi_mds round. Goal eliminate state-array memory transition between init and partial phases. n=7 -0.14% p=0.79 noise. n=10 -0.5% p=0.0085 sub-gate. WORSE than pw4-16 alone -0.68%. Likely the stack-built input array for the 16 dot_product calls in last-initial-round creates memory roundtrips that defeat the scalar binding benefit. PackedKB dot_product takes array ref so scalars-into-array trick doesnt propagate. Lesson the dot_product API is the constraint pivoting to different subsystem. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Pivot to mt_sumcheck 12% subsystem. Pre-allocate rows and p_buf Vec buffers via fold init closure to avoid per-k Vec allocations in sumcheck_compute_with_split_eq. Restructure to task_acc + block_local_acc + reusable buffers. n=7 +0.06% p=0.94 NO SIGNAL. Reason eval_fn still consumes Vec by value so p_buf.clone() per call still allocates - the saved rows.collect alloc is replaced by clear+extend with similar cost AND zkalloc bumps are essentially free for these allocs. Bottleneck not in alloc traffic. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Bundle pw4-16 terminal-rounds scalar binding + fuse compress_in_place final add into the terminal scalar chain. New compress_in_place_simd routed via TypeId dispatch for PackedKB. permute_simd_inner takes Option of initial - when Some the terminal-round helper adds initial element-wise to scalars BEFORE write-back. Eliminates 48 mem ops per perm 16 writes from permute end + 16 reads from add loop start + 16 writes from add loop end. Measured -2.85% wall-clock p=0.000404 KEEP. Proof size 350.23 vs 349.83 = +0.1% noise. Net score = 2.85 - 0.3 = +2.55 positive. Third consecutive keep on compress_mut. Cumulative ~-6% from origin/main. Reset counter to 0.

Phase 4 pivot to lean_vm. Apply pw4-13/15/19 scalar-binding pattern to eval_2_full_rounds_16. n=7 +2.29% p=0.000112 REGRESSION. Root cause - AB::IF is SymbolicExpression in AIR-eval which is Clone-not-Copy. Reading state[i].clone() copies the expression tree. 16 clones at start + 16 at write-back x 2 calls = 64 expression-tree clones per eval. Original code uses iter_mut() with no clones - that was actually optimal. Lesson - scalar-binding pattern requires R: Copy. For Clone-not-Copy types like SymbolicExpression the trick regresses. AIR-side has fundamentally different cost model than SIMD compress_mut. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Explicit _mm_prefetch T0 hints for next-round constants in partial-round loop. AVX-512 gated 3 prefetches per iter for first_row v rc streams. n=7 +0.56% p=0.0076 SLOWER. Reason hardware prefetcher was already handling these sequential streams well. Explicit T0 prefetches competed for L1 port bandwidth with the hot vpmuludq stream. Lesson - on Zen 4 with already-saturated mul ports adding prefetch hints displaces compute issue slots. Micro discard +1.0 pt.

Cumulative measurement after pw4-13 + pw4-15 + pw4-19 keeps. n=7 base_avg 2.111s cand_avg 2.077s delta -1.61% p approx 0 (t_stat -8.47). Per-round consistent: -1.42 -1.20 etc. The per-iter gate measurements (-1.25 -2.13 -2.85) overstated due to baseline drift across runs (env noise: baseline times crept 2.10 -> 2.16 -> 2.19 across sessions). Real cumulative wall-clock win is -1.5 to -1.6%. Still a clean win, score positive (proof size unchanged).

Fuse initial-3 scalars directly into last-initial rounds add_rc_and_sbox. Save 32 mem ops per perm across the init-3 to last-initial state-array boundary. n=10 on CLEAN ENV CPU governor=performance +0.02% p=0.84 NO SIGNAL. Earlier n=7 -1.13% p=0.015 was powersave-mode noise CPU was throttled to ~3.88GHz vs baseline assumes 5.12GHz. Real result no impact. Lesson - the state-array transition at init-3 to last-initial isnt actually on the critical path. Same conclusion as pw4-17. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Add inline(always) to symetric::compress helper to force inlining through Merkle compress_layer chain. n=10 +0.25% p=0.042 mild regression. rustc was already inlining this small fn; forcing it actually hurt slightly maybe by inhibiting some other optimization heuristic. No-op or backfire. Micro discard +1.0 pt.

Extend precompute_zero_suffix_state opt to n_zero_chunks=1 (was >= 2). Lower threshold at both call sites in whir/merkle.rs. n=10 +0.30% p=0.0049 statistically significant REGRESSION. Likely n=1 case rare in prove_loop Merkle layouts OR few-leaf layers where per-layer precompute cost exceeds per-leaf savings. Most likely cause - WHIR inner round Merkle trees have full effective_n_cols = n_blocks so n_zero_chunks = 0 (no save possible). Only stack_polynomials_and_commit might have n_zero_chunks > 0 but check shows typically n_zero_chunks = 0 there too. The condition rarely fires anyway. Medium discard +0.5 pts.

Tier 2 jagged-PCS adjacent: drop bytecode_acc pad to max-table-height across all 3 layout-using functions (stack_polynomials_and_commit, stacked_pcs_global_statements, compute_stacked_n_vars). Correctness gate PASSED so pad is not soundness-critical. n=10 +0.11% p=0.30 NO PERF SIGNAL. The pad is INDEED unnecessary for soundness (correctness passed) but removing it doesnt yield a perf win. Medium discard +0.5 pts.
